data.summary: The primary cause of the slow pod startup was the `model.download` phase, which took 53.369 seconds out of a total startup time of 61.0 seconds. This delay is due to the application downloading a 524MB model from a remote model hub on every pod startup. The model weights are stored on an ephemeral `emptyDir` volume, preventing cache reuse across pod restarts.

findings.statement: The total pod startup time was 61.0 seconds, exceeding the SLO threshold of 10.0 seconds.
The `model.download` span was the dominant factor, taking 53.369 seconds.
During the `model.download` span, 524,288,000 bytes (524MB) were downloaded from `http://model-hub.kubesage-infra.svc.cluster.local/weights-500m.bin`.
The `cache_hit` attribute for the `model.download` span was `false`, indicating the model was not loaded from a local cache.
The model directory `/work/model` is mounted from an `emptyDir` volume named `work`, which does not persist data across pod restarts.
The `app_init` phase, which includes the model download, took 54.683 seconds.

ruled_out.reason: The image pull duration was 4.184 seconds for 53,328,919 bytes, which is a minor portion of the total startup time and indicates a reasonable pull throughput of 12,745,918 bytes/s.
The image pull throughput was 12,745,918 bytes/s, which is not indicative of a slow registry or network.
The scheduling phase took only 1.0 second, and there were no failed scheduling events, indicating no capacity issues.
The readiness probe duration was 0.647 seconds, which is a small fraction of the total startup time and occurred after the `app_init` phase completed.

recommendations.rationale: To prevent repeated model downloads, keep weights on a persistent volume, pre-populated by a prefetch job, and enable the app's cache reuse. This will allow subsequent starts to load from local disk.
